name: Christ in the Old Testament
about: Types, shadows and prophecies fulfilled in Christ.

teachings.title: Two birds, cedar, scarlet and hyssop
teachings.summary: The cleansing sacrifice of Leviticus 14 and Isaac on Moriah picture Christ, so everything in the law pointed to Him and the Jews are without excuse.
teachings.text:
Of course the sacrifice recalls [Genesis 22](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/1782) Abraham and Isaac, and the purification sacrifice laid out in [Leviticus 14](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/1949), the mount in Jerusalem being where Abraham brought his son. Issac who carried the wood up the hill. God providing the ram, caught by the head in a thicket of thorns.

We see God tell Moses that the sacrifice for him that is to be cleansed *two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.*

We see the wood of the cross, the scarlet of the blood, and the hyssop, the same used by the Roman guard to give Jesus the vinegar to drink.

We see one bird placed in an earthen vessel, as Jesus was placed in flesh. We see it sacrificed and burned, its blood put on the living bird, which is then set free.

Everything points to Jesus and everything in the law was a picture of Him to come, so that the Jews would have no excuse.

teachings.title: The cleansing birds, cedar, scarlet and hyssop
teachings.summary: Isaac's offering and the Leviticus 14 cleansing ritual both picture Christ, showing all the law pointed to Him.
teachings.text:

teachings.title: The leper's cleansing birds a picture of Christ
teachings.summary: The Leviticus 14 ritual for a cleansed leper, with the slain bird in an earthen vessel and the living bird released, is a detailed picture of Christ's death and resurrection.
teachings.text:
Next Luke gives us an example of the healing that is a theme of his gospel, being a physician, in this the healing of a leaper who shows great faith and humility "*Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean."* Again, a picture of the manner in which we are saved. Calling upon the mercy of the Lord to make us clean, with the faith to know He is able to.

Jesus heals him, and cautions him to keep the manner of it to himself, but to go to the temple and offer the sacrifice for cleansing from leprosy given of Moses, found in **Leviticus 14**.

It is a complicated ritual, one that must have seen little use in the times it was given in the law, as leprosy is untreatable and the healing from it coming only from a miracle. Yet Moses in the Spirit gives the process in the law, with specificity. I quoted only the first part of the ceremonial sacrifices, but it takes up basically an entire chapter. But nothing in the Bible is accidental, coincidental or incidental.

First the leper goes to the preists who will send one out of the camp, out to the wilderness, to check the man and confirm they are healed. A testimony given, as Jesus says here.

Then the priest must take two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop, and place one of the birds in an earthen vessel, and kill it, sprinkling the blood of the dead bird on the living bird, the wood, the scarlet cloth and the hyssop, and then sprinkle the blood from these items and the living bird on the healed man, 7 times, proclaiming him clean, and releasing the second bird to the wild.

The bird in the earthen vessel, the clay that man is made from, as a substitutionary sacrifice, its blood upon wood, like the wood of the cross. On the scarlet, as the garments of Christ were so stained. On the hyssop, like the sprig dipped in vinegar, given to Jesus on the cross. And this blood of atonement then cleanses the man, and the living bird, like the risen Christ ascends to the heavens.

The other sacrifices require lambs without blemish, etc, and are equally pictures of Christ Jesus. It's a fascinating chapter to read and study on. Placed in the OT that a testimony of Jesus could be made when he healed this man.

teachings.title: The passover lamb and the Lord's supper
teachings.summary: The Passover ordinance pictured Christ the Lamb, and at His last supper Jesus turned it into a new memorial ordinance, the Lord's supper, done in remembrance of Him.
teachings.text:
We find Jesus, now just one day from His crucifixion, very desirous to eat the passover. He mentions this desire repeatedly, telling His disciples to go and find such and such room, and prepare *where I shall eat the passover with my disciples.*

This is the first of the holy days of the year, which begins in spring in the Hebrew calendar, the first month *Adar*.
10 days in, the lamb without blemish is brought before the people, separated from the flock. On the 14th day the lamb is slain before the congregation. The blood spread with hyssop upon the wooden door posts, in remembrance of the first passover where this saved those within the home from the angel of death, given as an ordinance by God that in future generations when asked by those children, *What mean ye by this service?*  That they would explain the sacrifice, what it meant, and how God delivered the people with the blood of the lamb. That they cast out the leaven of their households, and broke and ate unleavened bread in remembrance of their flight from Egypt.

And ordinance is a memorial service, a ritual that is designed as a picture of something, to be kept as a reminder to future generations so they would understand.

*And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.*

God essentially saying, "Do this in memory of Me."

Jesus, intent to have this passover supper, before His betrayal and death, brings the disciples together, and immediately turns from the traditional Passover ordinance, the ritual observance with unleavened bread, the unfermented juice of the vine and the lamb, and gives unto them a new ordinance; what we call the Lord's supper.

Jesus being the lamb to be delivered to the high priests to be slaughtered. His body broken as the unleavened bread is broken. The cup of the fruit of the vine poured out, and divided, as His blood. Blood put upon the doorways of our hearts that we be saved from death. That it passover us.

The passover observance being a picture of Christ's death. The feast of unleavened bread, the forgiveness of sin. Being brought out of Egypt and to the promised land, a picture of our deliverance to the Kingdom of God.

This, Jesus last meal before betrayal, and in it He provides a new ordinance to be done in His memory, that when future generations may ask, *What mean ye by this service?* We have a ready answer.

The cup is the new testament in Jesus' blood, which is shed for us. The bread, His body that was broken upon the cross. We do this in memory of Jesus.

teachings.title: The tabernacle, a pattern of heavenly things
teachings.summary: Every part of the tabernacle is a picture of Christ and the Christian life: the freewill offering of accepting the gospel, the ark as the covenant written on our hearts, the shewbread as God's word, and the candlestick as the light of Christ.
teachings.text:
Transitioning from the previous chapters where the law of the covenant was given to the children of Israel and accepted in the blood of Moses sacrifices, God begins to instruct on the ceremonial ordinances, specific the building of the Tabernacle. The tent dwelling of God among His people.

It is important to understand that everything in this is a picture of Christ and the spiritual application is of Christianity.

**Hebrews 9**
*23 It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.*

*24 For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:*

The sanctuary, or holy place made with human hands represents the spiritual.

God says take the free will offering of the people to build with. They have to willingly offer to build the sanctuary. Our free will acceptance of the Gospel.

Then, God starts His instruction with the Arl of the Covenant, which will be kept in the heart of the Tabernacle. Where His angels protect His word, the stone tablets of the law, which are now written on our hearts.

**Hebrews 10:16**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them*

And so here we see that this is where the covenant is kept; in our hearts, just as the Ark containing the old covenant was kept in the heart of the Tabernacle.

We see that it is the mercy seat, the seat of judgment of God, overseen by His angels, just as we as believers are.

**Hebrews 8:5**
*Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.*

Next God instructs that a table be made before the Ark, and on it the shewbread, bread left daily in the Tabernacle and temple. The daily bread, which is God's word.

**Deuteronomy 8:3**
*And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.*

Then the candlestick, with the 7 candle holders, a picture of the light of Christ. The light of life. The 7 candles, the 7 spirits of God.

**John 8:12**
*Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.*

Jesus has the 7 spirits of God; the Spirit of the Lord, and the Spirits of wisdom, of understanding, of counsel, of might, of knowledge and of fear of the LORD.

And God says again; *And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.*

teachings.title: Blue, purple and scarlet
teachings.summary: Every detail of the tabernacle, from its colours to the veil torn at Christ's death, points to Christ and is not irrelevant to the believer.
teachings.text:
Blue, purple and scarlet, the so-called royal colors, were key to the design of the Tabernacle and come up frequently in the building of the Temples. The colors of the bruises and blood of Christ, by which we are healed.

The instructions for building the Tabernacle, the layers of curtains or walls of the tent, from the dainty fine linen cunningly stitched to the rugged, inside and out. The qualities of a man. The holy of holies at its heart. The law of God and His promise kept there in the Ark. Behind the veil. The veil which tore in twain at the death of Jesus, the separation from God and man done away with.

Everything in the Old Testament is pointing to Christ. including this. It may seem like an Ikea assembly manual and in the view of modern theologies that strip Christ from the "Jewish Bible," the Old Testament becomes meaningless and seems irrelevant to the believer. But every aspect matters. Every detail. Even the color and size and shape.

teachings.title: The half shekel ransom for souls
teachings.summary: The equal half shekel atonement paid by rich and poor was a memorial pointing to Christ, the ransom price paid for all our souls.
teachings.text:
Exodus chapter 30 continues laying out the physical tabernacle and carnal ordinances and diverse washings for Aaron and the priesthood, the incense altar and the holy oils and perfumes for anointing, as well as curses on those who fail to keep God's instructions regarding them, or who profanes the holy things.

We see that it is gold that makes the altar precious, and myrrh and frankincense for the anointing oil and holy perfume; a picture of the gifts given Christ by the three wise men and His holy being.

But God takes a slight detour from the ordinances of Aaron and his sons, to an offering given among the people. That when the people are numbered, an offering of half a shekel be given for every, on top of tithes, as an atonement offering. A ransom for their souls. Everybody paying the same price. No more no less, rich or poor. That it may be a memorial unto the children of Israel before the Lord.

This requirement being a memorial, through the generations to come across the centuries, pointing to the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh to be the actual ransom for all. A picture of the price paid for the atonement of our souls.

*For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.*

Amen

teachings.title: The meat offering a picture of Christ
teachings.summary: The unleavened, anointed meat offering pictures sinless Christ, and the salted firstfruits picture the saved, preserved by the Holy Spirit and spared the fire.
teachings.text:
The first several chapters of Leviticus, which lays out the Levitical priesthood and its ordinances and practices, deal with the subject of sacrifice for atonement and oblations, gifts given to the Lord of meats, which in Biblical terms is foodstuffs, not just flesh of an animal.

As we see in chapter 1, this is the holocaust or burnt offering of the lamb without blemish. The blood carrying the atonement. The sweet savour of the fire roasted fats and meats being pleasing to the Lord.

And this is a picture of Christ. Just as are the meat offerings in chapter 2. Everything in the Old Testament does.

Here we see the gift offering of fine flour, anointing oil and frankincense. The bread, representing Jesus, made without leaven, leaven representing sin.  Note that it was both raw ingredients baked by Aaron and his sons. Or finished cakes and wafers. Cooked or baked. And the priests eat thereof what is left over. The frankincense consumed completely, all anointed with oil, as befitting a King.

*And the priest shall take from the meat offering a memorial thereof, and shall burn it upon the altar: it is an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord.*

Showing the Israelites the truth of their savior in these ordinances. As a memorial to Him that was to come. All burnt upon the fire.

But the oblations of the firstfruits shall not be burnt in the altar. And all the meat offerings of the first fruits are to be salted generously. To season it completely as it is the salt of the covenant with God.

This represents the saved, the firstfruits of the harvest. The salt, the holy Spirit.

*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men*.

Salt is a seasoning, increasing the savour of the food, enhancing it. But it is also a preservative, keeping food fresh, longer. In this way, the Spirit acts in the believer. It isn't burned in the fire, just as believers are spared Hell.

God makes a provision for the corn given in a meat offering to be as the flour or unleavened bread, anointed with oil and frankincense, to be burned as the other flours, as a cornmeal, that there be no confusion.

teachings.title: The burnt offering: free will and substitution
teachings.summary: The burnt offering was offered by a man's own voluntary will as a substitute for his sin, refuting Calvinism and the Orthodox and Catholic errors on atonement.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 1:3-4**
*If his offering be a burnt sacrifice of the herd, let him offer a male without blemish: he shall offer it of his own voluntary will at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the Lord. And he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering; and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.*

Just to review something I meant to point out yesterday; note that the burnt offering is both of a man's own free will, and is an offering for substitutionary atonement.

Not a man chosen before time by God. Not some elect men, who are drawn and compelled to offer it. But by his own voluntary will.

And this offering was in his place for the payment of sin. It was the faith in God that held the remission of sin, the blood and the fire that was a picture of that faith, showing the pattern of things in Heaven.

This is yet another blow to Calvanism and to the damnable heresy taught by the Orthodox Church that there is no substitutionary atonement with Christ, and the strange and contradictory attempt by the Roman Catholics to square vicarious penal atonement, which is the Biblical doctrine as we see reflected in Leviticus, and their own existing heresies, mainly from Augustine and his progeny.

Jesus, the lamb without blemish, sacrificed for our sins. A propitiation that takes away the sin of all who voluntarily trust on Him for our salvation.

teachings.title: The bloody sacrifices show the cost of sin
teachings.summary: The gory sin offerings, slain by the sinner's own hand, showed Israel beforehand that the cost of sin is death, fire and blood, fulfilled in Christ's passion.
teachings.text:
Running behind a little bit but luckily for us, the New Testament is the best study guide for the Old.

We see that they sent offerings are given not only by the people but by the priest. And provides an opportunity for those in good conscience who may through ignorance violate the law. But later come to know that they did and seek forgiveness.

This is just as a child is born sinless and until the knowledge of the law comes, until they know right from wrong, send isn't held against them by God. It is only the knowledge of the law that kills us in sin. And it's only from that knowledge that we come to understand we need a savior. As Paul writes in **Romans 7**:

*For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died. And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death. For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.*

Now again the sacrifices are being given by God to the Hebrews as a sign of the Christ to come. He will fulfill all of the different oblations and propitiations. But we should note how bloody this is. How gory. That the man seeking forgiveness for himself or his immediate family is laying his hand on each sacrifice at the door and slaying it before the Lord.

This is a gruesome reminder of what Christ will go through. We have the entire account of his passion from four gospels and still it's difficult for us to comprehend. Now imagine a people before Christ. Looking forward to the cross. And we see in this way God is showing us exactly how the cost for our sin is death and fire and blood.

teachings.title: The cleansing of the leper points to Christ
teachings.summary: The law for cleansing a cured leper, a seemingly impossible event, is full of pictures of Christ and served as a testimony that a prophet, the Son of God, was among them.
teachings.text:
I have covered the symbolism and importance of the law of leprosy, and the atonement offered at the cleansing of one who is cured in another post [here](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9168).

It is fascinating to me that an incurable disease is given a process by God for ritual cleansing in the case of a leper who is cured.

There were cases in the OT of leprosy being "cured." In **Numbers 12**, after Aaron and Miriam gainsay Moses for marrying an Ethiopian, God curses Miriam with leprosy for 7 days.

The other instance is in **2 Kings** 5, where a captain of the Syrian guard, Naaman contracts the disease, and the Syrian King sends him to the king of Israel asking him to heal his servant.

*And it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me.*

As we see, it was as if he had asked him to raise the dead. An impossible task and the king worried that it was a provocation for war with Syria. But the prophet Elisha heard of it and said;

*And it was so, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.*

It's a wonderful story of faith and shows the power of God, highly recommend reading it.

But we can see that the idea that one could be healed from leprosy would have been something that the Israelites would have thought impossible save by God.

And yet an entire chapter is devoted to this unlikely thing, filled with imagery of the sacrifice of Christ. A picture of Jesus saving sinners from death. And the purpose of the practical application, as we see Elisha say, is to let people know there is a prophet of God among them.

Jesus heals the leper and sends him to the temple to perform this ritual, as a testimony unto the priests, that the Son of God was here.

teachings.title: The scapegoat and the sin offering
teachings.summary: On the day of atonement the slain goat pictures Christ and the scapegoat the remission of sins carried away and remembered no more.
teachings.text:
As for the two goats, brought before the Lord and lots cast to determine one to be the sin offering, whose blood was given to take away the sins of the children of Israel, the other made the scapegoat, who would be led to the wilderness and let go.

The lot cast are the **Urim and Thummim**, the means by which God "spoke" through the high priest. The sin offering a picture of Jesus, the scapegoat a picture of the remission of sin, brought away from the congregation and left in the wilderness to be remembered no more.

**Jeremiah 50:20**
*In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.*

The high priest would place his hands upon the head of the scapegoat and confess the sins of the people, that the goat would carry them, *all their* *transgressions in all their sins*.

**Hebrews 8:12**
*For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.*

teachings.title: The camps of Israel and the throne of God
teachings.summary: The four standards of Israel's camps around the tabernacle mirror the four living creatures around God's throne in Ezekiel and Revelation, because the tabernacle was made after the pattern of the things in heaven.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 4:1-9**
*After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald. And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold. And out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and there were seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind.*

*And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle.*

*And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come. And when those beasts give glory and honour and thanks to him that sat on the throne, who liveth for ever and ever...*

**Ezekiel 1:3-10**
*The word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was there upon him. And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire.Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man. And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass. And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings. Their wings were joined one to another; they turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward.*

*As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle.*

**Ezekiel 10:14**
*And every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.*

**Numbers 2:1-2**
 *And the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, Every man of the children of Israel shall pitch by his own standard, with the ensign of their father's house: far off about the tabernacle of the congregation shall they pitch.*

Each camp, Judah, Ruben, Ephraim and Dan had a banner. And each banner, and ensign; also called a symbol or crest.

The camps surrounding the Tabernacle containing the Ark of the Covenant, the throne of God. His mercy seat. The creation of which was a pattern shown Moses, reflecting the things in Heaven.

**Hebrews 8:1-5**
*Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man. For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.*

teachings.title: Jerusalem, where God placed His name
teachings.summary: Jerusalem and Mount Moriah, where God chose to place His name and provided the ram for Isaac, point to Christ, the name God placed there to be sacrificed and to reign.
teachings.text:
Jerusalem, was chosen by God to "place His name";

**Deuteronomy 12:5, 11**
*But unto the place which the LORD your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come...Then there shall be a place which the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dwell there; thither shall ye bring all that I command you; your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, your tithes, and the heave offering of your hand, and all your choice vows which ye vow unto the LORD*

The OT scriptures repeatedly say that Jerusalem is where God chose to place His name. Where the Son of God would be revealed. Where His name would be killed for our transgressions:

**Isaiah 53:3–5**
*He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not. Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.*

The same place Abraham was told to bring Isaac, at Mount Moriah, Zion:

**Genesis 22:2**
*And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.*

But God did not require the sacrifice of man, but rather gave His only begotten Son:

**Genesis 22:8**
*And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.*

In this place, where the altar was made, and the son was to be sacrificed, where a ram without blemish was caught in the thick of thorns was provided, Abraham recognized it for what it was:

**Genesis 22:14**
*And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.*

The place where the temple would be, pointing to the Messiah:

**1 Kings 8:28–29**
*Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day: That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place.*

God says that His promise to David that the anointed one would come from his line, and His determined use of Jerusalem as the city where He would place His name, is the only reason He did not wipe out Judah as He did Israel.

**Isaiah 37:34–35**
*By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

**Zechariah 9:9**
*Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.*

There, in Jerusalem would He place His name, Christ Jesus. The Alpha and Omega. The Lord of lords and King of kings.

**Isaiah 9:6**
*For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.*

teachings.title: Not a bone of Him broken
teachings.summary: Psalm 34's unbroken bones, fulfilled at the cross and pictured in the Passover lamb, show that all scripture points to Jesus and that God keeps His prophetic promises.
teachings.text:
In addition to the worship and praise of God, the recognition that His burden is light and He rewards us for bearing it, and the comfort that in our suffering and trouble, He is there, working it for good, **Psalm 34** contains a prophetic verse of Christ;

*He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.*

**John 19:31–37**
*The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away. Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe. For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken. And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.*

Nothing in Scripture is incidental, accidental or coincidental. And ultimately, everything points to Jesus.

**Exodus 12:46**
*In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.*

The Passover lamb being a clear type of Christ, the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The instructions repeated again, to emphasize the importance:

**Numbers 9:12**
*They shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinances of the passover they shall keep it.*

The picture of Christ given throughout Old Testament scripture shows the power of His word, knowing the end from the beginning.

**1 Corinthians 1:27–29**
*But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence.*

There is no wisdom of this world that can explain the prophetic nature of scripture. It is foolishness to those that reject the truth. Yet the sheer overwhelming number of things which are not that become things that are, shows the glory of God and the folly of man.

 And the faithfulness of prophecy shows us the power of God to keep His promises, and increase our faith. Amen

teachings.title: The sign of the prophet Jonas
teachings.summary: The tomb was empty before dawn Sunday after three full days and nights, fulfilling the sign of Jonas, and getting this timing wrong opens the door to worse error about Christ's suffering.
teachings.text:
Now, the first day of the week in the Bible is what we call Sunday. This finishes establishing the timeline of Jesus' death, burial and resurrection. Following 3days and nights, *before* dawn Sunday morning, Mary comes and the tomb is empty, Christ has risen already. The "night" is not yet "over," being yet dark. Wednesday night, Thursday night, Friday night. Thursday, Friday, Saturday.

*But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.*
...
*Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish's belly, And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.*
*For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.*
*Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head. I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God. When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.*
*They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy. But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord.*

It's a minor doctrine, the timing of these things, and yet its corruption and basic misunderstanding lead to all kinds of heresy and error. The day of the week isn't really important, but what Jesus did in that time is.

Often false teachers will use misunderstanding and error to build other, more damnable doctrine. Such as Jesus didn't suffer in Hell as a burnt offering for sin. Such as He didn't do so for 3 days and nights as the Bible says, making some doubt scripture.

Nothing in the Bible is incidental, accidental or coincidental. All scripture is valuable for doctrine.

teachings.title: Coats of skins: the first promise of Christ
teachings.summary: In Genesis 3 God promises the seed who bruises the serpent's head and covers Adam and Eve with skins by shed blood, a picture of Christ's imputed righteousness.
teachings.text:
So having sinned and fallen, God the Father who loves man, offers the first promise of Christ, while laying out the consequences of bringing sin into the world.

To the devil, that old serpent, *Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.*

I plan on expounding on the seed of the woman/seed of the devil, Revelation 12 and how this promise is fulfilled in Jesus in another post.  But note that the seed who bruises Satan's head, and whom Satan bruises the heel, is Christ.

To Eve, *I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.*

Women know pain and complications of childbirth in ways few creatures in creation can. And their season of fertility, more frequent, and their conceptions, multiplied. And by their nature, they shall desire their husbands will.

This last part deserves its own post as well. Both the meaning and implications of this desire, and how man's failure subverts and damages relationships, twisting this God given inclination in woman. (I would also note modern Bible versions change this verse to have opposite meaning, and how that undermines everything).

And to man, through Adam, we are punished;

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

The consequences of sin is death. We return to the ground whereof we were made, after a lifetime of labor to feed ourselves and survive. With the very things of nature we had dominion over, turned against us. Struggle. Death. The wages of sin.

But here, in **Genesis 3**, at the very beginning of mankind as a fallen creature, loved by God, He covers our sins.

 *Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.*

Shedding of blood for the remission of sin. Covered by the righteousness of the lamb, slain before the foundation of the world. God gives them this gift, freely. Of His own handiwork, not ours.

And so we are now, still naked. Still in sin. Our nature, made manifest in Adam, to choose struggle and death over obedience. Unable to cover our shame by our own works, and needing instead the gift of God, the blood of Christ, covered in the spotless coat of the lamb, slain without blemish. Given the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ as a gift from a loving and merciful God.

This is the Gospel. This is the same faith, as received by Adam, and passed on to his descendents, who call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, and becoming sons of God.

 *But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*

Amen

teachings.title: The seed of the woman bruises the serpent's head
teachings.summary: Revelation 12 fulfils Genesis 3: the devil, cast out, wars against the saints in the great tribulation while Christ, bruised on the heel, comes to crush his head.
teachings.text:
A murderer from the beginning, father of lies, the accuser of man before God in Heaven, with enmity with all of mankind, through Eve.

 Waiting to devour man all men, like a ravenous lion, and to devour Christ as soon as He was born though a child of the devil, Herod.

The devil is finally cast out, a 3rd of the host with him, and they fall. Shut out of Heaven and knowing their time short, they begin the great tribulation, to murder as many of *the remnant of the seed which kept the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus.*

Christ Jesus, the ruler of a rod of iron. Come to establish the Kingdom. Who, as a man on the cross, was bruised on the heel, but in the resurrection came into glory. Come to bruise that old serpent's head.

The three and a half years of great tribulation begin with his fall.

Because he is a murderer who hates mankind, hates Jesus. Hates God. And his seed are those who do too. Reprobates. They will make war with the saved, sons of God. And they will remain faithful unto death, having overcome in the blood of Christ.

It's one story. Genesis to Revelation.

teachings.title: God will provide Himself a lamb
teachings.summary: Abraham's offering of Isaac on Moriah pictures Christ in every detail, from the wood carried uphill to the ram in the thorns.
teachings.text:
and it came to pass after these things, God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, behold, *here I am.* (Remember this for later)

Take thy thou only son whom you lovest, take him to the land of Moriah (2 Chronicles 3:1 tells us that Moriah is where Jerusalem is). And offer him there for a burnt offering (Jesus three days and nights in Hell) upon one of the mountains which I will tell the of (Golgotha?)

On the third day, (obvious), Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place a far off. (Jesus lifting up his eyes rising up from hell)

I in the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you. (Abraham had no doubt that even if he slay his son that God would resurrect him).

And Abraham took the wood of the burned offering and laid it upon Isaac his son and he took the fire in his hand in a knife and they went both of them together. (Isaac the sacrifice carrying wood up the hill of Golgotha in Jerusalem)

Behold the fire and wood but where is the Lamb for burnt offering? And Abraham said *God will provide himself* a lamb for burnt offering. (God literally is providing himself as the lamb for the burnt offering. That's carefully phrased, don't miss it!)

And Abraham stretch forth with his hand and the knife to slay his son. And the angel of the Lord called unto him out of heaven, and said, abraham, Abraham: and he said *here am I.* (*Here I am* is where you brought yourself. *Here am I*  is a place where you've been brought)

And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad neither do thou anything unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou has not withheld by son, thine only son from me. (Again. Note Isaac isn't Abraham's only son, he has an older son Ishmael, God is being precise for a reason, this is a picture of Jesus)

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns and Abraham went and took the ram and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son. (From the crown of thorns to being the burnt offering in place of Abraham's son, God placed his only begotten son)

teachings.title: The Woman's Seed and the Serpent's Seed
teachings.summary: Revelation 12 fulfils Genesis 3: Eve's seed is Christ who crushes Satan, while Satan's seed are the reprobate who persecute those who overcome by the blood.
teachings.text:
Moving to the second half of Revelation, we take a step back, and in the more symbolic vision of John, we have what is essentially the fulfilment of the Genesis 3 prophecy, Eve, the mother of man, bringing forth her seed, even Jesus Christ, the Son of man.

The enmity of the serpent and the woman, his seed and her own. She bringing forth the man child who will crush Satan's head, he seeking to devour Him as soon as He was born.

The seed of Eve is man, and through her, Jesus. The seed of Satan are his spawn, reprobates. Sons of Belial. Twice-dead dogs. Vipers.

*Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.*

And so Satan tempts the earth and brings against all man tribulation. Going before the throne of God accusing man night and day. And knowing the Christ was born, sought to destroy Him through Herod, killing all the male children.

Ultimately, by the Jews who were Satan's seed, bruising the heel of Jesus, in death, only to see Jesus rise triumphant, overcoming the world with the keys to Hell and Death. And those sons of men who held the testimony of Jesus overcame through the blood of the Lamb.

And so it has been, Satan accusing and tempting the world, he and his wicked seed persecuting those who have overcome by the blood of Christ, and destroying mankind at every opportunity, like a ravenous lion.

But, as the end comes he will be cast out by Michael and his angels, and will be loosed on the earth for a short time to do his worst. This is the Great Tribulation, and for a 3 and a half year period, making war on the saints and overcoming them. But they who love not their lives unto death shall be saved....

teachings.title: Zacharias Prophesies the Promise Fulfilled
teachings.summary: Zacharias shows in the Spirit that all the prophets' promises to Abraham, Moses and David are fulfilled as John prepares the way of Christ.
teachings.text:
We learn that Mary spent the remainder of Elizabeth's term with her, and departed. John is born and so named, as the angel instructed Zacharias.

When people who know them hear this, they question why. And when mute Zacharias writes in faith that his son's name is John, he is freed from the curse and able to speak again. And the Holy Ghost comes upon him, and he gives praise to God almighty, prophesying in His name;

*Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us; To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham, That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear, In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways; To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins, Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us, To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.*

This is the promise of the Lord given witness by all the prophets. Don't miss this. Zacharias is showing, in the Spirit, how all is being fulfilled. With the mercy of God is with them. That his son shall prepare His way. To give knowledge of salvation, by the remission of sins. A light. A guide. Showing the way of peace. Because in sin, man is at enmity with God. But in Christ, God is offering peace on earth, goodwill towards man.

This is what was promised Abraham. Moses. David. All the prophets, up to and including John. Jesus is come.

teachings.title: Son of David and Son of God
teachings.summary: Luke's genealogy places Jesus in David's line as the promised King while He is also the Son of God, the two sonships of one who is fully God and fully man.
teachings.text:
Luke, having established the time and circumstances surrounding these events, then gives his version of the generations of Jesus, going from his stepfather Joseph's lineage. Perfect in his generations, all the way back to Adam, who we are reminded, was begat of God.

Being the son of Joseph, even adopted, places Jesus in line for the throne of David, fulfilling the prophets sayings that there will be a King from the root of Jesse, a descendant of David, who would rule and reign forever. The Son of David.

To the more secular, this places Jesus in line to be an earthly king. To make the Christ the physical deliverer of Israel. But to those called by the Spirit, and given understanding of scripture, the savior of their souls and heir to the Heavenly Kingdom. The Son of God.

It is these two sonships that Jesus was born into. Fully God. Fully man. And the conflict in the hearts of those who hear of Him, even those who directly saw Him walk among them performing miracles and preaching on the Kingdom of God, would set the stage for His ministry.

teachings.title: This day is this scripture fulfilled
teachings.summary: Reading Isaiah 61 at Nazareth Jesus openly declared Himself the Christ, and when His own rejected Him He pointed to the Gentile widow and Naaman, prefiguring God's turn to the Gentiles.
teachings.text:
Now having established somewhat of a following throughout Galilee, Jesus returns to Nazareth, the town He grew up in. Where He lived as a child with Mary and Joseph, His half brothers and sisters. Where He developed the habit of going to synagogue. He returns full of the Spirit, and is called to read, and He preaches the prophecy of Christ from **Isaiah 61:1-2**
*The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;*

Note He leaves off the day of vengeance. That is His second coming. Here He is at His first.

**John 3:17**
*For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.*

And so, Jesus reads this scripture foretelling His coming, and says, with every eye on Him; *This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears*.

For those who doubt that Jesus ever proclaimed Himself to be the Christ, here He is saying precisely that. From the beginning. In no uncertain terms.

And the crowd becomes incredulous. "Is this not the Son of Joseph?" They knew Him, watched Him grow, saw Him in synagogue.

In response we are given the first record of Jesus preaching in Luke;

*Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country. And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.*

In **Mark 6**, we get more detail of this part; *A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.*

Basically, those who know us best, whose familiarity has them over comfortable in their understanding. Many Christians can relate to this, where after being born again we try to share the good news with relatives or friends, and they, knowing us intimately, scoff. "You? I saw you that one time..." Or even just see us as the child they watched grow and can't accept that you've got something to offer them in your youth. It's why it can be difficult for a Christian to get members of his own family saved.

And so, being rejected of His hometown crowd, Jesus doubles down and preaches even harder, using scripture. He says, citing **1 Kings 17**, you remember Elijah, how he was rejected and shut up the heavens that it didn't rain for 3 and a half years? That in Israel was great famine? The Spirit led the prophet to a Gentile widow in the land of Zidon who, along with her son was about to die of hunger, having only one meager meal left between them. God sent Elijah there because of her faith. In the story she offers the food to the prophet in faith, even though it was all she had. And God works a miracle where they are all fed and sustained with what little she had until the time of famine was over.

Jesus says, I bet there were many widows starving in Israel. But it was a Gentile woman who He saved.

Then, Jesus mentions **2 Kings** 5, and the prophet Elisha, where a Syrian, the captain of the hosts of the army of the king, suffered leprosy. Jesus says that many lepers were in Israel in the time, but it was this Gentile that God sent His prophet to heal.

That the prophets were rejected of their own, and so the healing power of God, His blessings and promises went to others. To Gentiles.

**John 1:11**
*He came unto his own, and his own received him not.*

Jesus spitting fire, using scripture, He rebukes and reproaches His countrymen for their rejection of the word of God, the Gospel of truth He's brought to them, in a prefigure of the rejection He would face of the Jews at large, and prophesying God's turn to the Gentiles that would receive Him. And in a like manner, the crowd engaged at their own sin being pointed out, gathered to kill Jesus. They bring Him to the top of a hill, looking to cast Him off headlong.

teachings.title: Jehovahjireh: the Lord will provide
teachings.summary: Abraham's offering of Isaac on Moriah, with the ram provided in his place, pictures God providing His only begotten Son as the sacrifice for sin.
teachings.text:
*Jehovahjireh*, the Lord provides. And *as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.*

The sacrifice of the only begotten to be a burnt offering. The wood, carried up the mount, which is Golgotha, in the land of Moriah, which is Jerusalem. The thicket of thorns on the young ram without blemish, offered in place of the son by God.

God created a covenant with Abraham based on the blood of Jesus Christ. The sacrifice that God provides, to take away the sins of the world. The symmetry and perfection of His promises, laid out over thousands of years, and continues to this day.

Jesus is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world, that sinful man may be reconciled with God.

Jehovahjireh.

teachings.title: Thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter
teachings.summary: Zechariah 11 prophesies judgment on Judah's false shepherds and the breaking of the covenant, and his price of thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter is fulfilled in Judas' betrayal of the Good Shepherd.
teachings.text:
Continuing in Zechariah, we see the prophet turn from active encouragement in previous chapters to a more negative message and future prophecy against Judah.

The doors of Lebanon, the cedars, the oaks of Bashan, which is the fertile eastern bank of the Jordan, these represent the built temple, the great city Jerusalem, forged by the timber from these areas. Zechariah is prophesying their destruction, when reconstruction has hardly even begun.

The leaders, the shepherds, howl at their loss, the young lions roar, because the pride of Jordan is spoiled by false teachers and bad leadership at the judgment of God against them.

These wicked leaders, God says, slay the people and hold themselves not guilty. They sell them into servitude and think they are bless by the riches that comes to them for the price of men. The shepherds have no pity for their flock.

And God says this is His judgement on the Jews. Sort of the flip side of **Jeremiah 3:15**

*And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding*.

So, Zechariah preaches the destruction of the people at the hands of their neighbors and the kings and the Lord will not deliver them as He has so many times. As He just had from captivity. This is a future event.

God will feed the flock to the slaughter.

This all could be a prophecy of 70AD and the destruction of Jerusalem. The temple, as Christ said would come. Not on stone standing upon another. The scattering and spoil of the pride of the Jordan. The burning of the cedars and oaks. Or dual fulfilment with the days of vengeance, the end times prophecy of the destruction of Israel.

**Luke 21:21-22**
*Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

The prophet takes up two shepherd staves, and on one staff he writes "Beauty" and the other is called "Bands."

He says three shepherds he cut off in one month, and that he hated them and they hated him. False teachers, it seems. I can't say if this is Zechariah rebuking them, and taking their followers away from them, or God speaking directly that He did this to them. Either way, the flock of Judah is then cut off.

He breaks the staff "Beauty," which is the covenant with the people. Note the poor of the flock who believed on Him knew this was the word of the Lord. As a prophecy of Christ, and the new covenant that was established, the poor knew Jesus was the Word of the Lord.

Then he asks the people for his price as shepherd, and they set it at 30 pieces of silver. The parallel is obvious.

**Matthew 26:14-15**
*Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver*.

The good Shepherd, valued at only a lowly sum, 30 pieces of silver to be betrayed. And says to cast the sum to the potter.

**Matthew 27:3-7**
*Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.*

The act of throwing the money to the potter was a symbolic rejection in Zechariah, and the purchase of the potter's field with the money is the fulfilment.

teachings.title: My God, why hast thou forsaken me
teachings.summary: Psalm 22 prophetically gives Christ's cry from the cross, when bearing the sin of all mankind as our scapegoat and High Priest He was forsaken by the Father that we might live.
teachings.text:
*Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?*

In the 9th hour, Jesus cried out from the cross the words of the Psalm, the opening line of a song of desperation, penned by David centuries earlier.

An event recorded twice in the gospels:

**Matthew 27:46**
*And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?*

**Mark 15:34**
*And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?*

The man Christ Jesus, after a day of betrayal, abuse, beaten beyond human recognition, scourged, shamed and mocked, cursed, hung on the tree, and become sin for all mankind, acknowledging in death that, by taking on all of the sin in all of creation, He is, in that moment, no longer looked upon by the Father Whom He has been with, and a part of, since everlasting.

The prophetic words of the Psalm, Christ's words echoed through time to the psalmist, words Jesus Himself knew from before the foundation of the world, conveying the heartbreaking moments before the perfect and holy Lord would willingly give His life that we may live.

Jesus cried out in Aramaic, the daily language of the people, the language He grew up in life speaking, conveying His humanity in that moment.

The Hebrew words, long sung by Israel in the congregation, translated, and again, interpreted into Greek, and given to us in English, never losing a scintilla of power. Given to us as the blessed hope, an example of the endurance and steadfastness we should look to:

**Hebrews 12:2-3**
*Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds*.

Jesus, our scapegoat, receiving our sin in atonement, without the camp. Taking them utterly away. Not as the blood of bulls and goats, offered yearly for sanctification by the High Priest of the Tabernacle, but once and for all, shed for man. And He, as THE High Priest, entered into the Heavenly Tabernacle, and applied His own precious blood upon the mercy seat in Heaven.

No greater love than this has ever been shed towards us, that God became flesh, and lived among us, sinless and perfect, that He might drink of this cup. Going to the cross that we might live.

The tragic nature of these words reveals the depth of the love of God. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

teachings.title: Psalm 22 and the sufferings of the cross
teachings.summary: Psalm 22 prophetically pictures the mockery, piercing, thirst and parted garments of Christ's crucifixion and the anguish He bore all His life, before turning to the hope that all things work together for good to them that love God.
teachings.text:
The prophetic nature of the God-inspired Psalm of David continues, showing the children of Israel the truth of Christ, through a glass darkly. In David's personal pain, we see a shadow of the suffering of Jesus, a reproach of men, despised of the people, laughed to scorn.

**Matthew 27:39–43**
*And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads, And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross. Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said, He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.*

Compassed about by bulls, by dogs, men like lions, surrounded by the Roman soldiers doing the work of the Jews, piercing Jesus' hands and feet with nails. Splayed out upon the cross, His joints distended and twisted to support the weight of His body. The sinking feeling of death settling in His guts, as He struggled to breathe. His bones in sharp relief to His stretched out skin.

Crying out for water, Jesus is given vinegar to drink, raised up on hyssop, a bitter gall that could not quench His overwhelming thirst. The soldiers then parted His garments by lot:

**Matthew 27:34–35**
*They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink. And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.*

The desperation and loneliness, the mental anguish Jesus suffered on the cross, He had also carried with Him for 33 years. Understanding the suffering that awaited Him at Calvary, knowing His anointed part in the great redemptive plan, while at all points being touched by the infirmity of the flesh, and tempted as we are. His prayers at Gethsemane, Son to the Father, that if it were possible to take this cup from Him, please let it be so. But steadfast to do the will of the Father, even knowing the physical and emotional pain He would endure. These stanzas in this psalm tragically capture it all, before transitioning to the joyful hope found in every tribulation those who love God can take comfort in:

**Romans 8:28**
*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

teachings.title: Anointed with the oil of gladness
teachings.summary: The anointing of the king in Psalm 45 pictures Jesus anointed by the Spirit without measure, exalted after the cross, who gives believers the anointing of the Spirit by faith.
teachings.text:
After establishing His love for righteousness, the text states that He is anointed with the *oil of gladness* and that His garments smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia.

As messianic prophecy, the elements of His anointment listed are symbols of Jesus, His death and His triumph over death.

The oil of gladness, olive oil, used to anoint kings and in celebration. To freshen the face, and to signify joy.

We see throughout scripture that oil is used as a metaphor for the Spirit. And Jesus, at the start of His ministry is anointed by the Spirit from the Father, showing to John and the other witnesses that Jesus was the Christ.

**Matthew 3:16-17**
*And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.*

While earthly kings were anointed with physical oil, Jesus was anointed directly by the Holy Spirit without measure.

**John 3:33–35**
*He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true. For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him. The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.*

And so, the ultimate joy, the true anointing Is given to Jesus the Christ.

**Philippians 2:8–10**
*And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth*

The meekness of the sinless Son of God, going to the cross, despising the shame to be raised into glory, as the King of righteousness. The truth by which we are set free.

**Isaiah 61** says that He that was anointed by the Spirit of God to *preach good tidings to the meek..bind up the brokenhearted...proclaim liberty to the captives,* and to give unto them that trust in that truth..*.the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.*

The Messiah, the Anointed One, the Christ gives us the anointing of the Spirit by faith, that we may be His fruit, the trees of righteousness, planted that He might be glorified.

teachings.title: Melchizedek, a picture of Christ
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: Melchizedek, priest of the most high God with bread and wine and receiving tithes, pictures or is Christ, showing the patriarchs' faith was always about Jesus.
teachings.text:
As always, the New Testament is the best study guide for the Old Testament. Here Paul gives us understanding into who exactly Melchizedek king of Salem, priest of the most high God was, or at least pictures; Jesus Christ.

The appearance of Jesus throughout the OT, when the LORD speaks in person to the patriarchs, is called a "theophany," and most believers see Jesus in the "angel of God" passages throughout Genesis, the Lord who meets with and speaks to them, who appears to stop Abraham's hand sacrificing Issac, who wrestles with Jacob, appears in the fiery furnace in Daniel...Many such cases. As the Bible itself is one story, telling us about God, Jesus, the Holy Ghost and the Godhead's relationship with man, Jesus appears in every book of the Old Testament, regardless of manifestation.

And here, Melchizedek is seen as an early appearance of Jesus, taking tithes from Abraham, the king of peace, the preists of the high God. Without a beginning or end, no mother or father given, *made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.*

And his use by Paul as an example of a non-Levitical priest, to whom tithes and honor are due, that he was a pattern of Jesus and the preisthood of believers of Christ Himself. Showing that the less was blessed by the greater, saying *Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand.* Melchizedek, *whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.*

I believe it is Jesus, personally. But either way, it's a sign that the ordinance of bread and wine, of faith in God as savior, as the faith of the patriarchs, that it was always about Jesus.

teachings.title: Come Boldly to the Throne of Grace
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: Because Christ is a High Priest tempted like us, believers go boldly to God through Him alone, with no need of saints, Mary or sacraments.
teachings.text:
*Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession. For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

Having established that Jesus is God, Who created all things but was made by the will of the Father a little lower than the angels, made flesh to suffer and die for our sins, we can know that we have a High Priest, an advocate, who isn't some lofty god uncaring of our foibles and weakness, but Who at all points was tempted as we are, and through Whom we may boldly enter before God, His throne of grace, seeking mercy and help in our times of need. With the knowledge that God understands and loves us. We may enter boldly because we have such a High Priest in Jesus, He is the only mediator between God and man. There is no other name under Heaven by which we may be saved. There is no work by our own hands which can save us. There is no doubt of our salvation to those that believe. We enter into His rest by heeding His word and believing it.

And so we see, there is no calling on a "saint," or "Mary" to intercede, to bring us salvation, or any works, rites or sacraments that saves us from death and Hell. There is only faith in God's word and His perfect work, done from the beginning. The Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

teachings.title: A Priest After the Order of Melchisedec
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: Christ is a High Priest after the order of Melchisedec, greater than Levi, and the change of priesthood disannulled the law of Moses.
teachings.text:
And so, having established Jesus Christ's nature and purpose and the order of things pertaining to salvation of grace, including the rejection of the Gospel of truth, Paul returns again to his thesis, directed at the believing Hebrews, that Jesus is our High Priest, after the order of Melchisedec. Different than the order of Aaron. Separate from those Levite-born.

By necessity of a better testament and through the eternal life of Jesus, who was sinless and without spot, both the priest and the sacrifice, He is our High priest promised in the Psalms.

Paul is building the case that they who were under the law but now are saved by faith in Christ have no need of the human preists given by Moses, and the sacrifices and carnal ordinances are done away with in Jesus.

Some call this replacement theology, the replacement of the Jews as the "chosen people of God," with the Holy nation created from all tongues and kindreds by those who believe. But, as we see by Abram's tithing to Melchizedek, the High Priest of the most high God. Melchizedek who blessed Abram, *and without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.*

The Levites are of Abraham. And in Abraham, paid tithes to the King of Peace. The ruler of Salem. The High Priest of God who is without beginning or end. Like unto the Son of God. The less paid honor to the greater.

This is an important concept for the early church, which had many raised as Jews. Paul is laying out the replacement. The disannulling of the law of Moses. *For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.*

He reasons that the Levitical preists were made such without any oath by God, but the Spirit through David made such an oath regarding Jesus, that He be made a High Priest after the order of Melchisedek. Another promise made by God who cannot lie. To whom we have our full trust in, and see Jesus as the surety of the promise of eternal life, and so we must accept His vows given through His word. And the implications thereof are clear;

*But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them. For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself. For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.*

Amen!

teachings.title: The veil rent: come boldly to the throne
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: The high priest entered behind the veil only once a year, but Christ's death rent the veil, so believers may come boldly before God at any time through Christ our high priest.
teachings.text:
Now to the narrative of events, following the deaths of Aaron's sons, God provided Aaron with an assurance that if he came before the presence of God, beyond the veil, under the ceremonial ordinances laid out; his sin offering, the linen robes and mitre that were holy, his washings, etc, that the Lord promises he will not be struck down as well. Remember, their sin was in adding to the ordinances their own doctrine, using strange fire and not the fire the Lord has provided.

And so the high priest would only enter the holy place, behind the veil, once a year to fulfill these sacrifices of atonement, first for himself and then all the people.

But when Christ had died, that veil was torn. As told by Matthew:

*And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent*...

And as Paul wrote of the veil and the unbelieving Jews:

2 Corinthians 3:14-18
*but their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away. Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.*

And so we know we may go before the Lord boldly, and at any time, because Christ is our high priest;

**Hebrews 4:14-16**
*Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession. For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

Because we have been made heirs, the sons of God and given access to the Lord by His grace and mercy, through faith in His Son;

**Ephesians 2:6**
*And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus*

For God is not slack concerning His promises.

**1 John 1:9**
 *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

teachings.title: Why do the heathen rage
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: Psalm 2 prophesies the rulers' vain rebellion against God's anointed, whom God raised up and set as King over the nations, warning rulers to kiss the Son and trust in Him.
teachings.text:
Why do the heathen rage? Why do people think they can go against God? Kings and rulers, presidents and prime ministers, popes and priests, all seek to be freed from the ways of the Lord, to do what they will.

Especially the religious and political leaders in the time of Jesus.

**Acts 4:27**
*For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together*.

They believed if they killed the Son, they would break the bands, Their bonds, and be free of God.

Jesus addressed this in a parable, about a Lord who planted a vineyard and lent it out to husbandmen to dress and keep it. And when the Lord sent servants to gather the harvest, the stewards beat and killed them. So finally, the Lord sends his son;

**Matthew 21:38**
*But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance*.

David prophetically writes of this here in **Psalm 2**.

But, it is folly. The Lord holds them in derision. He laughs at their vain efforts, because Christ, His anointed, rose again.

He set His Son upon Zion, and upon the throne.

**Acts 13:32–33**
*And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers, God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.*

Jesus' inheritance are all the nations of the world, and possession of the uttermost parts of the world. And as Lord of lords and King of kings, He will rule them.

**Revelation 2:26–27**
*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.*

This prophetic Psalm gives warning to the rulers of this world, reminding them of their place. That they serve at the pleasure of the Lord, and He will deliver vengeance.

It's an amazing and consistent message, across the entire Bible; The Christ is God's anointed, and Jesus is the Christ. All who believe on Christ Jesus shall be saved. His grace and mercy giving us the chance to serve Him in righteousness.

*Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.*

Amen

teachings.title: Myrrh, aloes and cassia on the King
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: The spices on the King's garments in Psalm 45 picture the gospel: myrrh His sacrificial death, aloes His incorruption and resurrection, and cassia His ascension and eternal priesthood.
teachings.text:
The anointing oil is based on olive oil, but contains the other spices for fragrance, myrrh and cassia.

**Exodus 30:22–29**
