*Moreover the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, Take thou also unto thee principal spices, of pure myrrh five hundred shekels, and of sweet cinnamon half so much, even two hundred and fifty shekels, and of sweet calamus two hundred and fifty shekels, And of cassia five hundred shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, and of oil olive an hin: And thou shalt make it an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary: it shall be an holy anointing oil. And thou shalt anoint the tabernacle of the congregation therewith, and the ark of the testimony, And the table and all his vessels, and the candlestick and his vessels, and the altar of incense, And the altar of burnt offering with all his vessels, and the laver and his foot. And thou shalt sanctify them, that they may be most holy: whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy.*

This ointment is given of God to sanctify, and make all that it is applied to, holy. But it was reserved for the items of the Tabernacle and the High Priest, a holy anointing oil.

**Exodus 30:32**
*Upon man’s flesh shall it not be poured, neither shall ye make any other like it, after the composition of it: it is holy, and it shall be holy unto you.*

God also instructed not to anoint a stranger with this, as it is holy, threatening to cut off any who do it from the people.

Yet it is this holy oil, reserved for the things of God and His High Priest, that is given to the King described in **Psalm 45**.

Myrrh is a bitter resin extracted from a thorny tree, that was primarily used in burial preparations. It was given as a gift for a King by the wisemen visiting the infant Jesus.

Nicodemus used myrrh and aloes in the preparation of the body of Christ at His burial.

**John 19:39–40**
*And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight. Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.*

There is a sense of the suffering of Christ, the death He tasted for all men, in the application of myrrh in the Psalm, reflected in the Gospels.

The scent of myrrh on the King carries with it His majesty, that cannot be separated from His sacrificial death. His garments carry the scent of His ultimate act of love.

The aloes mentioned are not the oil we know today, but the fragrance made from an eaglewood tree, and those aloes are found in Nicodemus' mixture. Because aloes were used to preserve bodies and counteract the smell of decay, they symbolize resurrection, healing, and incorruptibility of Christ, in His death.

**Psalms 16:10**
*For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.*

Cassia is an aromatic bark, like cinnamon, and is used in the holy anointing oil, mentioned above. This ties in to the understanding of Christ not only as King but High Priest.

Taken together, these three spices combined on the garments of the King paint a complete picture of the Gospel narrative. Myrrh as the sacrificial death, aloes His incorruption and resurrection, and cassia, Jesus' ascension, and role as High Priest, forever.

And so in **Psalm 45**, as the King approaches His bride, He carries with Him the literal aroma of redemption. The scent of His gospel. Amen

teachings.title: The Judge of all the earth at Abraham's tent
teachings.theme: Christ appearing in the Old Testament
teachings.summary: Comparing scripture, the Lord who ate with Abraham was Christ, since no man has seen the Father and Jesus is the Judge of all the earth.
teachings.text:
*And the* Lord *appeared unto Abraham.*..This is an Old Testament manifestation of Christ Jesus, appearing with two messengers, angels of the Lord before Abraham on their way to judge Sodom and Gomorrah.

Seeing them approach, Abraham recognizes Him, and runs to prepare a meal, and give hospitality to God and His angels.

We can know this is Jesus, by comparing scripture with scripture. *No man hath seen God at any time, the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.*

But as we have seen repeatedly in the OT, the Lord, the word of God, and here, "Judge of all the earth" appears before Abraham and Sarah, talking with them and eating. Abraham recognizes Him right away.

The Bible says Jesus is the Judge of all the earth.

**Acts 10:42**
*And he commanded us to preach unto the people, and to testify that it is he which was ordained of God to be the Judge of quick and dead.*

**2 Corinthians 5:10**
*For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.*

As the Bible says in James 5, *behold, the Judge is standing right at the door.* Just as He was before the door of the tent of Abraham, on the plains of Mamre, West of Sodom.

There, the Lord reiterated the promise and the blessing to Abraham, that he and Sarah will have a son. That their seed will bless all nations.

We've covered that the seed is singular, Christ Jesus.

Sarah laughs, *After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?* and in a way familiar to us from the Gospels, and recognize in our walk with Him, He calls her on it and when she denies it in shame, He gently chides her, *Nay; but thou didst laugh.*

There is nothing beyond what the Lord can do. *At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.*

teachings.title: Jacob wrestled with God face to face
teachings.theme: Christ appearing in the Old Testament
teachings.summary: The man who wrestled Jacob was Christ, who renamed him Israel, a picture of being born again.
teachings.text:
And so, Jacob having prepared his own ways to protect what he has is now alone in the wilderness.

And there, he finds himself wrestling with a man, and there wrestled with him until the breaking of the day.

Jacob, an old man by our standards. Likely 60-70 years old at this point. Having been a rancher for decades, but still not a young man, endures this wrestling all night unto morning. And as the dawn came and the man saw he was in a stalemate with Jacob, touches his thigh and shrinks the sinew of his hip and lames Jacob, and doing this says "Let me go." Essentially telling the exhausted and now hobbled Jacob to give up and surrender. And Jacob defiantly says no, "*I will not let thee go, except thou bless me."*

The man asks, "What is thy name?"

"Jacob."

*And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed*.

*And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore is it that thou dost ask after my name? And he blessed him there. And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.*

The man he'd wrestled with all night was Christ Jesus, God in the flesh. And having overcome, was born again, given a new name. (As Jesus we know is want to do)

Face to face with God, halted and lame for his experience, he is blessed as a prince, inheritor of the blessing, recognizing God come in the flesh. And he passes through the river Penuel, a sort of baptism, the sun rises to warm him, Israel goes to meet his fate.

teachings.title: My presence shall go with thee
teachings.theme: Christ appearing in the Old Testament
teachings.summary: The angel and presence that went before Israel was Christ, the way we can come to the glory of God without being consumed.
teachings.text:
*And I will send an angel before thee; and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite: Unto a land flowing with milk and honey.*..

This is both a picture of, and literally IMO, Christ Jesus. God with us. Who appears to Moses, face to face even as God says He can't be seen in His full glory. Even as we have God the Father talking about His inaccessibility, the ordinances for the Tabernacle and diverse washings. That Moses will see only His hinder parts, for the glory of God is too much for man to see.

But in Christ Jesus, we are able to go boldly before the Father. The veil of the temple torn. *My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.*

Jesus is the way we can come to the glory of God without being consumed. Amen

teachings.title: Psalm 45 and the conquering King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45, inspired by the Holy Ghost, prophesies Christ the bridegroom King whose truth, meekness and righteousness are the qualities believers should pursue.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 45** is a doctrine-rich wedding song, that speaks clearly of the Lord Jesus, a bride brought to Him, and the promise of exaltation for the King of Kings.

Of course, the dual nature is both a historic royal wedding song and a profound Messianic prophecy, the Psalms often capture both layers in a way that makes them relevant to our lives as believers. It is a testimony to their divine inspiration.

The same inspiration described in the introduction found in verse 1.

The author says his heart is inditing a good matter, meaning fit to burst with the understanding he is speaking of. His *tongue is the pen of a ready writer.*

God has given him the idea, the words, His inspired, God breathed need to speak and record the word of God, that is bubbling our of his heart.

Jesus said *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh*, be it the evil of the Pharisees or the inspired word. Whether the penman, or those who have committed the word to our hearts.

**2 Peter 1:21**
*For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

And so, moved by the Holy Ghost, given the word of God, the ready writer gives us a song of romance and prophecy. Deeply layered and rich, as only scripture can be.

A similar song to Solomon's, messianic prophecy couched in a romantic allusion.

Verse 2 begins the description of One, fairer than all men, full of grace, blessed forever by God. The Christ. His chosen. The groom, and King.

Girded with His sword, the most mighty. Almighty. A name of God given this person. All glory and majesty are His.

Riding majestically, and prosperously, upon a horse to battle.

**Revelation 19:11-13**
*And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God*.

He has the word of God proceeding from His lips. Destroying the enemies of God with His sharp sword. The strength of His right hand, teaching *thee terrible things*.

What a picture that's painted. What a powerful, Almighty Son of God. Who comes to smite the enemies of His Father, and rule with a rod of iron, but His prosperity is in His truth and meekness and righteousness.

The terrible things, are in this context, the fearful lessons of the Lord. And these are grounded in those three qualities. The truth of the word, the meekness of our Savior, His righteousness in all things.

For the Christian, these three qualities are what we should pursue. We should gird ourselves with the sword of Truth, knowing His word in our hearts, ready to deliver it.

**Hebrews 4:12**
*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

Living in meekness, a servant. Condescending to men of low estate, that they may be saved. Putting our heart to The afflicted, the widow, the fatherless, the poor. For the meek shall inherit the Earth.

And living in righteousness. Doing right things by the judgment of God found in His word. Cleansed by the blood and carrying the righteousness of Christ within us. Being holy, as He is holy.

*Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

Truth, meekness and righteousness means loving what is good and hating wickedness. This is the inheritance of the Lord and the perfection of it found in Christ Jesus.

**Hebrews 1:8–9**
*But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

teachings.title: Forget thy father's house: the bride of the King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45 pictures believers as the bride of Christ, called to love Him above family and nation as a wife leaves her parents, and to look not to earthly lineage but to the spiritual children they win to the gospel.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 45**, the messianic wedding song, we transition from the King to the bride.

At His right hand stands the queen, decked in gold from Ophir, (a site somewhere south-southwest of Jerusalem renown for its gold).

Her ornamental beauty, provided by the King, to set apart the bride. The honorable women, the church.

As a picture of believers, we see the Kings great desire for the beauty He has bestowed. He is truly Lord and we worship Him.

*Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house*

We are called to hear the appeal from Heaven, to consider and incline our ear (*faith cometh by hearing*), to forget our people and our parents, and to become His.

**Luke 14:26–27**
*If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.*

We are called out, to be His above our family or national bonds. To "hate" here doesn't mean to dislike intensely, as it does today. It means to not love as much, to not prefer over another. To love Christ more than even your kin.

**Matthew 10:35–37**
*For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household. He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.*

Just as a wife is called to separate from her parents and cleave unto the husband.

**Genesis 2:24**
*Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.*

Becoming the bride of Christ, cleaving unto Him, placing our love for Him above others. A wedding is a picture of this relationship that we have. It is given as a parable, that we may better know Him.

In our status as His, the great of every nation shall show us favor. Perhaps in the Millennial Kingdom, certainly not in this life. But when we have come into the inheritance, they will respect our rule because Jesus is their Lord, and we are His.

We are arrayed as a burden in gold and fine embroidery, the white garments of purity, the righteousness of Christ that covers us.

*With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king’s palace*

**Luke 15:10**
*Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.*

This is the celebration of salvation. And the future wedding supper we are called to.

*Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth.*

We will not look to our earthly heritage, the genealogies and lineage, but instead at those we have won to the Gospel, as children who rule and reign with Christ. It is our godly heritage, the spiritual children we present to Christ.

Looking forward to the future of those we have helped come to repentance. This is our vow to our Lord and Savior.

*I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever*. Amen

teachings.title: To your tents, O Israel
teachings.summary: Israel's rebellion against Rehoboam in 1 Kings 12 pictures the Jews rejecting Christ, and every man going to his own house in John 7 is its parallel.
teachings.text:
Every man went to his own house, the matter unresolved, reminds me of the verse in **1 Kings 12:16**:

*So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.*

In this account of the old kingdom being divided, between the northern tribes and Judah we see the people demanding that Solomon's son, Rehoboam who has just been anointed king, ease the enforcement of God's law, claiming it's too heavy a yoke to bear. They rebel, they kill the man sent by Rehoboam to collect tribute (picturing God the Father sending Jesus, and the Jews killing Him). They then name Jeroboam their king, (picturing men putting their faith in what they want, rather than what God tells us).

*So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.*..

This rejection led to God's wrath upon the northern kingdom, and their having renounced their inheritance, their portion of the promise in David, they were eradicated by the Assyrians.

This is a picture of the Jews in Jesus' day, some choosing to follow God's anointed, most choosing their own way, and thus divided, each returns to their own house to do as they will.

*O Israel, return to thy tents*, and *every man went unto his own house,* shows that this is a parallel passage.

teachings.title: God will provide himself a lamb
teachings.summary: Abraham offering Isaac on Moriah pictures God giving His only begotten Son, from the third day and the wood carried up the hill to the ram in the thorns.
teachings.text:
and it came to pass after these things, the god did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, behold, *here I am.* (Remember this for later)

Take thy thou only son whom you lovest, take him to the land of Moriah (2 Chronicles 3:1 tells us that Moriah is where Jerusalem is). And offer him there for a burnt offering (Jesus three days and nights in Hell) upon one of the mountains which I will tell the of (Golgotha?)

On the third day, (obvious), Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place a far off. (Jesus lifting up his eyes rising up from hell)

I in the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you. (Abraham had no doubt that even if he slay his son that God would resurrect him).

And Abraham took the wood of the burned offering and laid it upon Isaac his son and he took the fire in his hand in a knife and they went both of them together. (Isaac the sacrifice carrying wood up the hill of Golgotha in Jerusalem)

Behold the fire and wood but where is the Lamb for burnt offering? And Abraham said *God will provide himself* a lamb for burnt offering. (God literally is providing himself as the lamb for the burnt offering. That's carefully phrased don't miss it)

And Abraham stretch for with his hand and the knife to slay his son. And the angel of the Lord called unto him out of heaven, and said, abraham, Abraham: and he said *here am I.* (*Here I am* is where you brought yourself. *Here am I*  is a place where you've been brought)

And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad neither do thou anything unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou has not withheld by son, thine only son from me. (Again. Note Isaac isn't Abraham's only son, he has an older son Ishmael, God is being precise for a reason, this is a picture of Jesus)

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns and Abraham went and took the ram and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son. (From the crown of thorns to being the burnt offering in place of Abraham's son, God placed his only begotten son)

The name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen. (And it was amen)

teachings.title: Christ our Passover on the preparation day
teachings.summary: Jesus died on Passover preparation day, Wednesday, as the lamb without blemish, and the three Sabbaths that followed picture His doing all the work, the same faith in the blood that saved since Adam.
teachings.text:
Now again, we have the timing of things from John. This is the preparation day for Passover. It is the 6th day since Jesus supper with Mary and Lazarus, 5th day from the triumphant ride into Jerusalem on the weekly Sabbath, Saturday. This is the Wednesday of their week, Passover, a high Sabbath begins at 6pm. This aligns with the first Passover which was a picture of the Christ to come. The lamb chosen without blemish, brought before the high priest on the preparation day. Slaughtered and burned in a fire, a holocaust or burnt offering. His blood what saves those of us cloaked in it.

Passover day is followed by the high holy Sabbath of the feast of unleavened bread, Friday. Saturday is the weekly Sabbath. Three days without work, as Jesus does it all, we can do nothing. Healing us during Sabbath, just as He did so many times to the blind and lame during His ministry. It is why 3 days and 3 nights He will spend dead, in Hell, paying it all for our sin. This is the New Testament.

This is why these days were set by God in the Old Testament. This is the greatest of prophecy fulfilled. And the faith that saved in the Old Testament, the faith that saved since Adam, is in the blood of the lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

It's a beautiful picture of Jesus and the Gospel, of faith without works, of the same dispensation of salvation for all man's history. And so it's no wonder corrupt false churches teach none of it by their calendar.

teachings.title: Pentecost: the firstfruits of the harvest
teachings.summary: The feast of weeks was the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, fulfilled when three thousand were saved at Pentecost.
teachings.text:
Fun Fact regarding Pentecost:

The High Holy day, called the Festival of Weeks or "Shavuot," is 7 weeks following the second day of Passover (feast of unleavened bread). In Greek, Pentecost, meaning 50 days following Passover itself.

 Passover commemorates God freeing the Israelites from Egypt, Pentecost, the Feast of Weeks celebrates the day of the giving of the law by Moses and commitment of the people to agree to God's covenant and be His people, detailed in **Exodus 34.**

In the midst of chapter 34, almost as an afterthought, we find verse 22:
*And thou shalt observe the feast of weeks, of the firstfruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of ingathering at the year's end.*

As we know, at Pentecost in Acts, the Apostles and disciples receive gifts of the Holy Ghost, and begin preaching to the multitudes gathered in Jerusalem for the feast, and bring 3000 thousand to salvation.

Literally the first fruits of the harvest.

What an amazing God we have. What a blessing His word is.

teachings.title: Joseph's Brothers Hated Him as the Jews Hated Christ
teachings.summary: The brothers' resentment of Joseph's prophetic dreams mirrors the Jews' hatred of Christ, of whom Moses and the prophets wrote.
teachings.text:
And so, we understand the setting. They hate the favoritism Jacob gives his son, Joseph and that he's tattled on their sin. *They hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him*, and to compound matters, Joseph tells them of his dream.

*For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.*
*And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.*

In parallel to Christ, we see the resentment. Like Jews resentment of Christians, the older hating the younger because of the prophecy of who will reign. Not exact but echos. And Joseph dreams again.

*And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?*

Here Jacob interpreting the dream for us, that he is the sun and his mother, the moon. The brothers the stars. All bowing before Joseph. The brothers hated him even the more, but Jacob observed the saying.

The prophetic dreams about Joseph are from God, given by the Holy Ghost. We will see later how tied to dreams and prophecy Joseph is. But note the building resentment of the brothers mirrors Israel's resentment of Christ, where Jesus speaks to the Jews about how the prophets spoke of Him;

**John 5:46**
*For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me; for he wrote of me.*

**Luke 24:44**
*These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me*

They had the word of the prophets and hated Jesus because of it. In spite of it. Despite the truth of the prophecy being the hope of salvation, they hated the idea of bowing to Christ the Lord.

Joseph's brothers didn't understand that his dream of preeminence was to prophesy their physical salvation.

teachings.title: The Fall Feasts Picture the Second Coming
teachings.summary: The fall feasts of Leviticus 23 picture Christ's second coming, and their commanded rest from all work pictures salvation by grace without works.
teachings.text:
The Levitical feasts are also important to understand for our study of Revelation going forward. They are a picture of Christ. Last Easter I gave a rundown of the ways Jesus fufifiled the spring feasts, Passover, the feast of unleavened bread and Pentecost. These were a picture of His first coming. Likewise, the fall feasts God commands in **Leviticus 23** represent Christ at His second coming. The timing, the harvest, the gathering. The blowing of trumpets. The dwelling in houses made by God, while singing His praises. All point to end times Bible prophecy. ("Booths" were tabernacles, tents, made from branches and boughs, rough cut and gathered from nature). The timing of things mirrors events in Revelation, as we will see.

One incredibly important point of the feasts, these Sabbaths; NO WORK was to be done by the people. This is the reinforcement by God of His grace in giving us a free gift of salvation in Jesus, who is the Sabbath. Three days of no works, 3 Sabbaths in a row, from His crucifixion to His resurrection, Jesus doing all the work. And like the Spring feasts, the convocations or gathering of the congregation/church, there is no work allowed, for Jesus did it all.

*For whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people.*
*And whatsoever soul it be that doeth any work in that same day, the same soul will I destroy from among his people.*

These are those unsaved who are appointed to wrath. Notice it is both the unbelieving, those not afflicted by the atonement made by the sacrifice, and those who do any work who are cast out and destroyed. So too will it be in the second coming.

We should all be familiar with **Matthew 7:21-23**:
*Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

**Romans 4:6-8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin*.

**Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.*

teachings.title: Jesus the bread which came down from heaven
teachings.theme: Pictures of Christ in the Exodus
teachings.summary: The manna in the wilderness pictures Christ the bread of life, and in John 6 the unbelieving Jews murmured and took His spiritual lesson literally.
teachings.text:
In **Exodus 16** we find the recently freed Isralites, a month now out from bondage in Egypt, shown signs and wonders of God by Moses, murmuring that they were better off in chains. Having run low on supplies, their flesh in need afflicted their spirit.

But God hears their murmurs, and tells Moses and Aaron that he will send them bread to eat in the morning, and the flesh of quails at night. God sets the rules of His heavenly bread that each person takes the measure allotted, and uses it that day, and all would be filled. If they tried to store it up for the next day, it would rot, except for that manna gathered on the day before the sabbath, which would feed them both days.

And like the entire story of Exodus, we have a picture of salvation in Christ.

Jesus, who is the bread of life. Jesus, who is the sabbath. Our rest. Jesus who was sent by God the Father that all who believe on Him shall never hunger. Jesus is the rock from which the water springs as well, as we will soon see. And those that believe on Him shall never thirst.

In **John 6**, Jesus is preaching to the crowd that had followed Him to Capernaum, He had just fed the multitudes with a few loaves and fishes, that thousands were full and there was more to spare. Like in the wilderness of Sin, He fed them whether they followed God's laws or not, to prove them, that they may know He was of God.

But Jesus first chastises the multitude, saying they didn't come to Him for spiritual reasons, but because their belly was full.

And just as the children of Israel in the wilderness murmured against Moses, against God, here too the Bible says they murmured against Christ;

*The Jews then murmured at him, because he said, I am the bread which came down from heaven.*

And Jesus, being God, hears their murmurs and knows their hearts, and says; *Murmur not among yourselves. No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day. It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me. Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life.*
 *I am that bread of life.*

*Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead. This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die. I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.*

He is giving a spiritual lesson using the allegory of bread from Heaven, the manna in the wilderness, and applying it to His own body, which in death would take on the sins of the world that whoever believes on Him shall have eternal life.

But the unbelieving Jews, unable to understand Jesus take what He says literally and scoff; *The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?*

And knowing their hardened hearts and dull hearing, Jesus doubles down on His parable;

*Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you. Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.  For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed. He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him. As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me;  This is that bread which came down from heaven: not as your fathers did eat manna, and are dead: he that eateth of this bread shall live for ever.*

Get the context; Jesus had just preached a basic parable of salvation in Him, using the manna and Hia miracle the day before, as a picture of the spiritual application of belief and eternal life, and they couldn't understand it.

teachings.title: The sabbath rest and spring feasts picture Christ
teachings.summary: The sabbath rest pictures salvation by Christ's finished work rather than ours, and the spring feasts were fulfilled in Christ's death, resurrection and Pentecost.
teachings.text:
Now we are here in Leviticus chapter 23, and in it God provides the basic terms of the sabbaths and holy days to be kept by the children of Israel.

Understanding that sabbaths means rest, and that the prohibition of doing work on the sabbath is a picture of Christ Jesus, and the rest we enter into in Him. That we are saved by the rest given to us by the Lord and not our own works. That if a child of Israel works on these days, he is cut off, just as anyone trusting in their works for salvation is likewise cut off from the Kingdom of God. It is an undeniable truth that is repeated over and over again throughout the Bible, from the creation through Revelation. We are saved by Christ's perfect work, not our own. Not by being a "good person" or contrite or "trying to avoid sin" or how well we make "Jesus the Lord of our life."

Jesus paid it all in full, and the Spring feasts of Passover, unleavened bread and Pentecost all serve as ordinances to the Isralites as a picture of Christ.

I covered much of this in the Gospel studies, recently in [a study of Luke](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9753).

It is fascinating and amazing how God set this before the people and thousands of years later, we see it pay off with Jesus, the Passover lamb, slain on a sabbath, in Hell for 3 days and nights, all sabbaths, and risen again, only to ascend into Heaven on Pentecost, the feast of the first fruits held 50 days after Passover. The day in which the disciples went out to the multitude of gathered Jews preaching the Gospel in every tongue. The 5,000 saved that day being the first fruits of the spring harvest.

teachings.title: Christ the bridegroom and the whore of Babylon
teachings.summary: Scripture pictures God's people as a bride and idolatry as adultery and whoredom, which is why the Roman Catholic Church is shown as the whore of Babylon, mother of harlots.
teachings.text:
Throughout scripture, God's relationship to His people is likened unto a marriage, Christ Jesus as the bridegroom, believers the bride. And just as married couples are joined together, become of one flesh, and adultery an abomination, so too scripture refers to chasing after false gods and idols as adultery.

The fornication with which a man may put away his betrothed is a like symbol of God's putting away a people who have gone after strange gods. He also calls it whoredom.

Scripture says to suffer not a harlot of the daughters of Israel, and it is both literal and symbolic of the call by God to be faithful unto Him.

That is why the Roman Catholic Church, the Whore of Babylon, mother of harlots, is represented this way. The cup of her fornication. It's all relative in terms to the bride, the believers in Christ who remain faithful.

The institution of marriage itself is a parable by which God teaches us of fidelity, and what it means to be a jealous God. How the man is head of the house, one body and one flesh with his wife, just as Jesus is head of His body, made up of the saints.

The one world religion of works and many gods will be used by the beast to gain control, until they turn on the whore and install the antichrist in the temple, proclaiming himself as God, Christ returned.

teachings.title: He believed, and it was counted for righteousness
teachings.summary: Abram's faith in the promised seed was imputed to him for righteousness, and the sacrifices of Genesis 15 pictured Christ's blood offering.
teachings.text:
That's a lot of Bible this morning, and I didn't even get as deep as we could on this, but it's all fundamental to understanding the Gospel, and who is the seed of Abraham, how he blessed all nations. How through that seed, Abraham had multitudes too numerous to count as heirs to the promise made when he called upon the name of the Lord. The promise made when *he believed in the Lord; and He counted it to him for righteousness.* That his righteousness was imputed for that faith, by a gracious God. And it was faith in that seed to be given by the Lord, and the blessings for that heir and the promise made in Him.

As we will see in Esau and Jacob, the blessings and promises of the heir are important. The free will choices made by man, and faith in God determining who received them, not the law. For under the law the eldest received the inheritance. And the blessing.

*And he said,* Lord God, *whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?* And the word of God tells him to sacrifice *an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.*

Each a sign or a picture of Christ. As established in the Levitical laws, 400+ years from when this is happening, done to show they mercy of God in redemption by faith, in the blood offerings, the sin offerings, the burnt offerings. A testimony necessitates a blood offering. These were a symbol of Christ's.

And in a deep sleep, a darkness fell upon Abram, and the word of God said; *Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* prophesying the time to come and the sojourning to Egypt and enslavement. *And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.* Moses writing in the Spirit of the prophecy of Exodus given to Abraham.

*And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age. But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.*

The LORD telling Abram that he himself will die knowing peace, but that the land will not be given unto his descendants until the wickedness of the Amorites comes in. They are going to purge the land of Canaan of the wicked, as an instrument of the Lord. Against *The Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites, And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims,*
*And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.*

And a furnace and a lamp appeared on the offerings, passing between those pieces laid on an altar, a testament signed by God.

teachings.title: The World Hates an Evil Report of Sin
teachings.summary: As Joseph's brothers hated him for his evil report, the world hates faithful Christians because preaching against sin exposes their deeds.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 37** begins the tale of Joseph and Judah, the other brothers and how the sons of Jacob came to be in Egypt. The generations of Israel, told by God through Moses. In this narrative, there lays prophecy of Christ Jesus, both as a figure in Joseph and in the blessing upon Judah, which we will see later near the end.

But keeping in mind the picture of Jesus in Joseph and the traits of man in the brothers, especially Judah/Jews of Christ's time, there's a lot to digest.

First, we are given the timing and situation; Joseph, the first son born unto Rachel, Jacob's first love, and so the father's favorite. Joseph, out with his half brothers tending the flocks returns to his father, bringing an "evil report." Bringing word to the father that the children are in sin.

And the brothers hate him for it.

Much the same way today the world hates a faithful Christian for the reminder of their sin we bring. The light shined on their inequity. As Jesus says in **John 3:20**:

*For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.*

Christians standing fast against sin bring an evil report of the wicked hearts of men. The world resents it.

**John 15:18** I*f the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.*

Joseph's brothers hated him for the same reason. Sinners hate preaching against sin. Standards and morality. God's word, which convicts them. Christians who bring an evil report to their deeds.

And like Joseph's brothers, the world plots and schemes ways to shut us up. To sully Christ's name by our own failings. To discredit God's word. To subvert His people. To call good evil and evil good.

[Isaiah 5:20](https://t.me/ApeMtn37/3516)
*Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!*

teachings.title: The Whore and the Bride
teachings.summary: The whore and the Lamb's bride are set in contrast: trusting idols, rites or works is spiritual adultery against a jealous God.
teachings.text:
There is an interesting contrast made in the opening verse of chapter 17, and a verse from chapter 21:

**Revelation 17:1**
*And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters:*

Revelation 21:9
*And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife.*

The whore represents the unsaved and the wicked. The saved as the Lamb's wife, a bride.

The contrast and context of faithfulness and purity is intentional. A parable for a God whose name is Jealous.

*For thou shalt worship no other god: for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.*

As Jesus teaches in Matthew 5:28

*But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.*

The same is true for us spiritually. When we put other gods before Him, even in our hearts, or trust in something other than Him to be our Lord and savior, it is adultery.

To make your faith one of idols and rites and vain traditions, trusting in our works and institutions made of man over the Lord who bought you, it is whoremongering. It is fornication.

And all those who lead others to this, especially when they claim the name of Christ Jesus, are harlots. Whores. And they serve the beast.

teachings.title: Christ Offered Once to Bear Our Sins
teachings.summary: Substitutionary atonement teaches that Christ's blood, pictured by the old sacrifices, sealed the better testament and removed the veil between God and man.
teachings.text:
Substitutionary atonement, also called vicarious atonement, the Biblical understanding Jesus Christ being the sacrifice that takes away the sins of the whole world, to the salvation of those who believe, is laid out here (and throughout scripture) as the blood needed to affirm the promise made by God the Father. Just as the blood of bulls and goats was used to seal the covenant with Moses, or marked by Abraham with his promise from God.

But these sacrifices were for a time and a place and acted as a picture for the perfect sacrifice of Jesus Christ, Whose blood marked the promise of a better testament, one in which the separation from God pictured by the temple, the veils, the Levitical priests, dietary laws, marking of days and carnal ordinances of the Old Testament is done away with.

Here at the end of the world, Jesus was offered once and put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself. And in doing so, became our High Priest, and we who believe adopted sons, a holy priesthood. The separation from God is gone. The veil torn asunder.

Many false religions posing as Christians deny the idea that Jesus was the sacrifice that gave us the offer of God's mercy. They deny the grace of a loving God who bought them with the price of His Son. That the shedding of blood and the remission of sins isn't the way, but instead these thorns and briars produce evil fruit that cannot repent from dead works to serve the living God.

But the Bible teaches us the truth of the matter. That Jesus as the sole mediator between God and man was by the means of His death, becoming sin for the redemption of transgressions. (For sin is the transgression of the law).

A testament having no power while the testator liveth. And so the death of the testator signified that those called had come into their promised inheritance. Amen.

So Christ was offered once to bear our sins. And those of us who believed look to His coming to our day of redemption. The Spirit as the surety of the promise, a testimony within us to the truth of God's word.

teachings.title: Ordinances were pictures, not idols
teachings.summary: The Old Testament ordinances like the sabbath were shadows of Christ ended at the cross, but the Pharisees, like Israel with the brazen serpent, made the picture an idol and a work of self-righteousness.
teachings.text:
In chapter 5, and now again in Luke chapter 6, we see the Pharisees seeking to accuse Jesus, that they may discredit Him and His growing ministry. Particularly, they are seeking to shame Him and His disciples for their failure to keep certain ordinances, carnal ceremony, given both by tradition and under the law of Moses, among these ordinances are things like the fasting of meats(food), ceremonial washings(**Matthew 15:12**) and the keeping of the sabbath, the day of rest, as we see here.

The Bible says these ordinances were given in the OT as a picture, a shadow, to remind the people of the promise of the coming Christ, that they not forget and hold fast to the faith preached unto them, until the *day of reformation*. That is, until the things they are foreshadowing come true. Until Christ comes. At that time Jesus figuratively nails them to the cross with Himself. They are over and done, having served their purpose.

And, with the ordinances ended, the Bible says, so too was the regard God had for the nation of Israel. They were to either believe or perish, the same as the Gentiles. Thus the destruction of the Temple in 70AD, least any confusion remain.

And of these ordinances, the keeping of the sabbath was probably the most important, that the people would enter into God's rest, understanding that His work was finished at the time of creation. A picture man could understand, working 6 days and resting the 7th as God did. Forbidden work, because God did it all in regards to salvation. It is a picture of salvation by faith alone in His perfect, meaning complete, works, finished by the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

But man is simple, and foolish and superstitious. The things of God that are a physical picture of the spiritual application He seeks to teach us, becomes an end unto itself in vain tradition. Many, with an autistically literal approach, put the power in the picture, not the things that are being pictured.

And example is given in the OT, in **Numbers 21** where by unbelief the Hebrews in the desert were beset by poisonous snakes, fiery serpents. Many were bit and were dying in agony. God, as an object lesson in the Christ to come, had Moses lift up a brazen snake, made of molten brass and formed, upon a tall wooden pole. This represented Christ and the crucifixion, where Jesus became all sin for us. He said to the people if you look up on this picture of salvation you'll be healed. Lesson learned.

We know this was a picture of Jesus, because it was explained in **John 3**:

*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.*

But we are told that hundreds of years later, the Israelites had lost the purpose and understanding that this picture served. In **2 Kings 4** Hezekiah became king and had to right many of the wrongs in the land;

*He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.*

The picture of the spiritual became a physical idol. The Heavenly lesson became bonds of the carnal.

This is where the Pharisees, Sadducees and scribes are at in the time of Christ. They have lost sight of the spiritual application for these things, and worship the symbol instead.

And so the carnal ordinances were to them an idol. And the work of their flesh in keeping these things replaced their faith in the Lord. They became self-righteous. They used the keeping of these ordinances as how one becomes righteous, rather than faith in what it represents, the Christ to come. And so, they become holier than thou  hypocrites. And later, Judaizers seeking to impose their vain traditions on the newly born again Gentiles. Circumcision, sacrifices, and the keeping of holy days such as the sabbath.

teachings.title: The entire Bible teaches one faith in Christ
teachings.summary: What is mocked as replacement theology is simply the Bible's one theme of salvation in Christ from Moses to Revelation, which dispensationalism denies.
teachings.text:
The entire Bible teaches what is derisively called replacement theology. Better phrased; The entire Bible teaches the one faith of salvation and redemption in Christ. The failure of man in the flesh to find holiness in the works of their own righteousness, and the grace and mercy of God in providing a sacrifice for their sin that they may know Him. For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.

Moses wrote of Jesus, in Genesis. In Exodus. In Leviticus and Deuteronomy. The prophets spoke of Him, and preached His gospel of redemption and reconciliation. The Psalms sing of Him and His coming. Jesus Christ in the flesh spent 3.5 years of an earthly ministry reaching the lost sheep of Israel that He could lead who were His, calling them to repentance and preaching to the unbelieving that they were going to be replaced and cast into outer darkness with wailing and gnashing of teeth.

Once the veil is torn at the death of Christ, the remaining scripture teaches of the gospel given to a people who were not a nation, now heirs to the Kingdom. The branches that did not produce fruit meet for repentance, cast into the fire.

The epistles giving us the grafting in, the theology of salvation and religion undefiled. The Revelation of Christ Jesus, the rapture of believers, the resurrection, adoption and redemption God predestined in His Son. And God's final judgement that we may know it, and come to Him before it's too late.

And it is this simple truth, the entire theme of scripture, that the false doctrine of dispensationalism denies and rejects.

teachings.title: The Lord, merciful and gracious, and Jealous
teachings.summary: In Exodus 34 God reveals Himself as merciful yet not clearing the guilty and as Jealous, guarding His people, while the feasts all picture Christ.
teachings.text:
*Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost. And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent.*

Exodus chapter 34 finds Moses in need to hew the rocks into tablets to replace those he broke in his anger at the golden calf and the sin of the children of Israel. The first God hewn, now must be made by Moses that God could give to him the covenant as a record, written in stone.

Only Moses was allowed on Saini, not even the beasts of the field were allowed to graze the foothills nearby.

The Lord came in a cloud and the figure of Christ Jesus (IMO) appeared before him, as the glory of the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed "*The Lord, The Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.*

This is who God is. We who are saved seek to know Him and throughout scripture we are given many names and descriptions that allow us to understand the holy God. Here is the quality of God that is judgment. He is merciful and longsuffering. He forgives. But He does not clear the guilty, and he visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third or fourth generation.

That is not to say they are punished for the sins of the father, but rather their inequities being judgment upon their people for generations. God is about to declare a genocide of the people in the way towards the promised land. The wickedness they have done in His sight. The groves and high places, molten gods and altars. God tells Moses that they are to destroy these people that their wickedness doesn't infect the children of Israel, through practice, through marriage, or in any way including eating meat sacrificed to idols.

We learn a name for God and it is Jealous. He is a jealous God. Jealousy is not envy or covetousness. It is fiercely protecting that which one owns. God is saying in this covenant He owns them, they are His people. And if they go whoring after strange gods because they were snared by covenant to make peace with the people He has judged be destroyed, He will have vengeance upon the children of Israel.

To further defend what is His from whoredoms, going after strange gods, the Lord further emphasizes the ordinances for feasts He has put in place as a memorial for what He has done for the people of Israel, and as a picture of the Messiah to come, Christ Jesus.

The feast of unleavened bread that begins immediately after Passover, which is the sabbaths of Christ when He is 3 days and 3 nights in Hell for our sins. And because His only begotten Son is a sacrifice for us, and because the firstborn sons of the children of Israel were spared in passover, even if their cattle, they belong to God and must be attoned through a substitutionary sacrifice. All a picture of Christ.

The sabbath, again a picture of Christ.

The feast of weeks, which leads to the Pentecost. The firstfruits of the harvest.

Then the feast of the harvest at years end.

All a picture of the time to come, and a memorial for the children of Israel that they may know Jesus.

*Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning.*

The unleavened bread and unfermented wine of the Lord's supper. Taking Jesus down from the cross before sunset on Passover.

The first of the firstfruits are God's under this Mosaic law. All a picture of Christ.

teachings.title: Israel saved by the blood before the law
teachings.summary: Israel was delivered from Egypt by faith in the passover blood before receiving the law, so those who demand turning from sin before believing reverse God's order.
teachings.text:
Now the salvation of the children of Israel from Egypt, that are freed from the yoke of bondage, came in faith on the promise of God. That by the blood of the Passover offering they are spared death. That by the waters they passed through, baptized into a new people and brought to a land promised them of God. Flowing with milk and honey, a land taken by those who failed to fear and serve the living God, but set about to establish their own righteousness. And then sanctified by the Lord to His purpose.

This historical and physical story is a picture of the spiritual, and the individual salvation of us who believe and are adopted by God as His people.

And so we should notice the order of things; salvation is front loaded and found only by faith. For the salvation of Israel from bondage and death came by faith alone, by the blood.

The Isralites in Egypt were not told to change their ways first. To become holy first. To repent of their sins and throw themselves before God crying for mercy because of how wicked they were.

God decided in His grace to offer them mercy if they believed Moses and Aaron, and trusted in the blood of the lamb.

And so all Israel was saved.

Then they were baptized together. Then they were given God's law. Then they were told to sanctify themselves, for their own good and to better serve God's will.

Those who place the giving of the law before the acceptance of faith are in error. Those telling others they must turn from their sins first before they can believe are entangling them in bondage. Placing the yoke upon those who should be set free.

teachings.title: The shewbread and the Lord of the sabbath
teachings.summary: The lamps and shewbread picture God's truth and word, and religion that forgets their meaning becomes rote practice used to condemn, as with the Pharisees.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 24** begins with the command to have the lamps of the Tabernacle burn continually, dusk to dawn. A statute for ever. That there is light in the place of God.

And God commands that there be bread baked as a memorial, continually, as an offering before the Lord, and eaten by the Levitical priests. This is called the shewbread, concentrated by the Lord.

The light symbolizes the truth of God throughout the Bible, and so it is never dark before Him. The bread is both the life given the people by God's grace and His word.

This shewbread becomes a means of feeding David and his men as they flee Saul, who was in a murderous rage against the future king. Even as it was offered to God and holy, but to the Lord's purpose, it fed His favored in a time of need.

Likewise, as Jesus rebukes the Pharisees when He and His disciples gleaned corn on the Sabbath to eat, Jesus points to how these things are the Lord's, and not just blind tradition and meaningless ritual. That He is the Lord of the sabbath.

Often religion becomes rote practices, that forget the meaning behind them as the Pharisees had. Using these things to condemn. Jesus says had they understood who He was, that He was present for mercy in His death and resurrection to come, that the sacrifices of the temple were a picture of Him who had come not to condemn but to save, that they'd understand why it was acceptable for them to eat of their work, as the Levites were allowed on the sabbath. Because they did the work of God.

teachings.title: The jubilee pictures Christ's redemption
teachings.summary: The sabbatical years and jubilee picture Christ as near kinsman redeemer, with the trumpet of jubilee pointing to His second coming and our redemption.
teachings.text:
Leviticus chapter 25 brings us the law of Jubilee, a perpetual sabbatical observation of the 7th year, in the land of Canaan which the Lord brought the children of Israel, culminating in the 49th year, 7 times 7, a jubilee, a proclamation of liberty, wherein all God's children shall be redeemed.

Of course this parallels with Christ, and the redemption from the bonds of sin He makes for us, as the near kin, the Son of man, setting us free.

The particulars of this law, which wouldn't take effect for the Isralites until they had settled the land, driving out the former inhabitants and dividing by lot the tribes and the habitations thereof, showed not only the foresight of God's providence, but His terms as the actual owner, the land Lord so to speak, of the land He gives them.

And so, 6 years the fields are sown and the vineyards dressed, but in the 7th, there was no work to be done in the land. God promises them that the 6th year will be bountiful enough to tide them over to the 9th year, that they could live off their stores, because God provides all. Not of their own works.

The timing of the jubilee, which was marked in the 49th year, 7 sabbaths, was marked at the end of the fall feasts by the trumpets at the end of the day of atonement.

Just as Pentecost is celebrating the 7th sabbath after Passover, the spring feasts, represent Christs work here at His first coming, then the Jubilee is marked by the fall feast, which is emblematic of His second, and the day of redemption for believers. The trumpet sounds to announce the victory of the Lord, the atonement bought with blood, the redemption from bondage and the liberty given all, rich or poor.

teachings.title: Rahab and the scarlet thread
teachings.summary: Rahab the harlot was saved by her faith in God and placed in the line of Christ, her scarlet thread a picture of His blood, showing God can redeem anyone who holds the faith.
teachings.text:
And so we are here in **Joshua** chapter 2, and the newly anointed leader of the Hebrews is about to lead the people over the Jordan and into the promised land.

His first act is to send 2 spies to spy out the walled city of Jericho. This is similar to an earlier appearance of Joshua, in **Numbers 13**, where Moses sent 12 spies into the land, and 10 spies were bad and 2 were good.

Joshua and Caleb were the good men, who had faith in God to deliver the land to them. The 10 cast doubt and fear.

Not wishing a repeat, apparently, Joshua sends only 2, and these men make their way into Jericho by way of the home of the harlot, Rahab. There she lodges them and hides the spies when the king of Jericho sends out men to find them. The harlot hides the men upon her roof and sends the kings men on a fruitless search back towards Jordan.

She tells the Hebrew spies that she has done this because the whole land knows that the Lord God is with them, and are friegtened of them, considering the miracles of the Red Sea and the defeat of the other Canaanite kings. She has faith that the same Lord God will bring them victory in Jericho. The spies thank her, and she asks that they swear her family will be protected in their eventual siege of the city. The spies grant her an oath. That if she places the scarlet thread she had let them down on in her window, that all within her household will be saved.

Her faith in God to deliver the Israelites, and her faith in the promise of the spies, will lead to her salvation, as we will see in a few chapters. And the same faith serves as a picture of Christ. The scarlet thread, like the blood on the door frames on the first Passover. The same scarlet thread of the blood of Christ that runs throughout the Bible.

And Rahab is part of that bloodline of Christ Jesus, as we see during the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew;

**Matthew 1:5-6**
*And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias*

The Greek spelling of 'Rachab,' is Rahab. She birthed Boaz of Judah, who eventually begets David, in the human lineage of Christ. A scarlet thread.

And she is saved by her faith, we know. Despite being a harlot. Despite her sinful life. She is redeemed, and honored with a mention in the Hall of Faith found in **Hebrews 11**, in the company of great Old Testament believers;

**Hebrews 11:31**
*By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace*.

She is also used by James, alongside Abraham, in his examples of those whose actions demonstrated to others the faith she had in her heart;

**James 2:25**
*Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?*

Given as an example of faith by God, to show us that He may use anyone for His purpose, and redeem anyone who holds the faith.

teachings.title: I am my beloved's
teachings.summary: The bride's choice to rise early and go forth with her beloved pictures the mature believer deliberately making Christ the centre of each day and working with Him to bear fruit in new believers.
teachings.text:
Song of Solomon 7 opens with the King, having called his beloved Shulamite woman to return to him that he may look upon her at the end of chapter 6, now detailing what he sees of his beloved. He describes her beauty and the perfect symmetry of her body.

*How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!*

Everything he sees of her is good. Just as we are seen as perfect and without spot when God looks upon us, clothed in the righteousness of Christ.

**2 Corinthians 11:2**
*For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.*

**Colossians 1:22**
*In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

The woman responds to her husband, her brother, her spouse with unwavering confidence;

*I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.*

We are Christ's, and His desire is for us.

Beginning there in verse 10, she responds to her beloved, knowing she is his, and inviting him to go forth with her, to live with her. To get up early to the vineyards, to see the vine flourish and come to fruition, where she will give him her love.

The spiritual application here; She has gone from her initial humble acceptance of his love, to the joy of the wedding feast, to her period of complacency, persecution, profession of faith and renewal, to now making the decision to plan her day and life around him, is a beautiful picture of the Christian life.

A believer makes the conscious decision to make Jesus their companion. To go forth with Him and to reside with Him. To wake early in the morning, starting the day with Christ, and His word. In prayer.

This intentionality is contrasted with the bride laying in bed, hesitant to wake, making excuses to avoid letting in her beloved. As mature Christians, in it for the long haul, we seek Him first.

We work with Him to tend the vine, which is His church, bringing forth fruit which are new believers. Planting the seed of His word. Watering and nurturing. Tending to them, the babes in Christ, and helping them grow to maturity. Through it all, giving Him all our love.

We lay up our fruit, those people we have given the gospel to, the needy to whom we give comfort. The broken hearted we have consoled. This treasure we have laid up for Heaven, but to Him is the increase. We give Him our all because He is our beloved.

teachings.title: Jesus is the excellent name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Psalm 8 praises Christ, who is God, the Creator through whom all things were made, the I AM given the name above every name, and the only name under heaven by which men must be saved and worshipped.
teachings.text:
The excellent name of our Lord is Jesus.

**Psalm 8** is a song of praise for the Christ. The name of the Lord, who has been set by the LORD, God the Father, over all things. Who also is God.

Jesus is the anointed, Who is ordained to strength, and mighty.

**Hebrews 2:4–9**
*God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will? For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.*

The New Testament reveals the intent and interpretation of the Old. We see Jesus using Psalm 8:2 against the Pharisees, showing that He is the name of God;

**Matthew 21:15–17**
*And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were sore displeased, And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise? And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany; and he lodged there*.

Through His name was all creation made:

**Colossians 1:16–17**
*For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.*

**John 1:1–3**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.*

*The same was in the beginning*, when men first called upon the name of the Lord.

**Genesis 4:25–26**
*And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

Jesus has been made to have dominion over all things, that the glory and honor be given to Him.

**Ephesians 1:9–10**
*Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him*

And the excellency of His name is revealed in Christ Jesus.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus is the name of the Lord. Of the great I Am.

**John 8:56–58**
*Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad. Then said the Jews unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham? Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.*

No other name is given by God to be worshipped as God.

**Acts 4:12**
*Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.*

teachings.title: Christ the King of all the earth
teachings.summary: Psalm 47 prophesies Jesus, who is God, ascending with a shout and returning with a trumpet to catch up the saints, reign as King of kings over every nation, and finally deliver the kingdom to the Father.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 47** is a song of praise for the Lord, the King of kings. Christ Jesus, Who shall put every nation under His feet.

**Revelation 11:15–17**
*And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever. And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O LORD God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.*

He shall rule and reign with a rod of iron, and give to all His people their inheritance in His Kingdom.

Jesus is God. Verse 5 says *God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.* A prophetic Old Testament verse, made clear in the New Testament, carrying the comfort of all believers;

**1 Thessalonians 4:16–17**
*For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

We shall sing of the glories of the Lord, forever.

**Revelation 7:10–12**
*And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen.*

**Revelation 19:16**
*And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.*

For Jesus is the King of all the earth, and reigns over the heathen. All the nations. He is greatly exalted above every name.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus will reign over all things, and, having defeated death and been made ruler of all, He will give all to God the Father. A perfect sacrifice, holy and acceptable, made holy by His righteousness:

**1 Corinthians 15:24–27**
*Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him*.

**Psalm 47** is a wonderful and prophetic song of praise and worship for the Kingdom of God, under our Lord Christ Jesus. All honor and praise is His. Amen

teachings.title: Mount Zion, chosen of God
teachings.summary: Zion is holy because God placed His name there and separated it for His purposes, the place of Christ's sacrifice and future reign, not because its people are holy.
teachings.text:
Mount Zion, Jerusalem, is often referenced and praised as the place God chose to place His name. His holy city, the mountain providing natural protection on 3 sides, situated perfectly. A river running through the fertile valley. The setting where Abraham brought Issac. Where God prepared Himself a sacrifice. Where Jesus was slain and rose again, and where He will reign in the Kingdom to come.

The name, Zion, means a “monument; raised up; sepulcher,” the place of the tomb, hewn out of rock, the site of Christ's burial. Chosen by God.

Jerusalem, the city isn't a lonely peak, but rather a settlement nestled within a protective bowl of higher terrain, with Mt Moriah and the mount of Olives part of the limestone rings, defending the area.

**Psalm 125:1–2**
*They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever. As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.*

Beautiful for situation, a perfect location, the city if the great King on its north face.

**Psalm 132:13–14**
*For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.*

**1 Peter 2:5–6**
*Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.*

The shelter of Zion, the cornerstone of which is Christ, is where Jesus returns to in the end times, with the 144,000 witnesses.

**Revelation 14:1**
*And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.*

The defenses of this holy mountain were enough to dissuade kings and armies.

Sennacherib, of Assyria, the most powerful emperor of the ancient world, invaded Judah with a massive army of 185,000 soldiers.

He sent his top military commanders to the walls of Jerusalem, fiercely mocking King Hezekiah and blaspheming God, confidently expecting the city to fall just like every other nation before it.

Hezekiah called out to the Lord for protection of the city.

**2 Kings 19:16–19**
*LORD, bow down thine ear, and hear: open, LORD, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God. Of a truth, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands, And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.*

And God harkened to the prayer, for His own purposes and will;

**2 Kings 19:32–34**
*Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

Zion is defended for His own sake, because He placed His name there, and for the promise made to David that out of Zion shall come a King.

**Romans 11:26–27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Zion is holy, because it has been separated unto the purposes of God.

It is not holy because the people there are holy. God allowed Babylon to raze the city and remove the people. Jesus decreed that Jerusalem would fall, and in 70AD it did. With the end times approaching, the city is considered wicked;

teachings.title: Dark sayings made plain in Christ
